extracted.intended_audience: licensees, applicants, attorneys, carriers, practitioners, and parties appearing before the Federal Communications Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules governing filing, service, deadlines, representation, and conduct in FCC proceedings (how to compute filing periods, methods/timelines for filing and service, practitioner eligibility and discipline, petitions/appeals procedures, and related documentary requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for hand-carried filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents not required to be accompanied by a fee and which are hand-carried must be tendered for filing in complete form ... with the Office of the Secretary before 4 p.m., at the address indicated in 47 CFR 0.401(a). The Secretary will determine whether a tendered document meets the pre-7:00 p.m. deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-carried filings must be complete and presented to the Office of the Secretary before 4 p.m.; the Secretary decides if a tendered document meets any pre-7:00 p.m. deadline. (This contrasts with other timing rules for electronic filings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing receipt times
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed electronically pursuant to § 1.49(f) must be received by the Commission's electronic filing system before midnight. Applications, attachments and pleadings filed electronically in the Universal Licensing System (ULS) pursuant to § 1.939(b) must be received before midnight on the filing date. Media Bureau applications and reports filed electronically pursuant to § 73.3500 of this chapter must be received by the electronic filing system before midnight on the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic system receipt before midnight on the filing date is required; different electronic systems (general e-filing, ULS, Media Bureau) all use midnight receipt as cutoff unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of filing periods when filing period is less than 7 days (holidays not counted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided (e.g., §§ 1.773 and 76.1502(e) of this chapter), if the filing period is less than 7 days, intermediate holidays shall not be counted in determining the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a short filing period (<7 days) applies, do not count intermediate holidays. Examples illustrate computing first and last day and show weekends may also be treated as holidays per definition; apply paragraph (g) (short-period rule) before adding mailing days under paragraph (h) when both apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance of additional 3 days for mail service on short filing periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document is required to be served upon other parties by statute or Commission regulation and the document is in fact served by mail (see § 1.47(f)), and the filing period for a response is 10 days or less, an additional 3 days (excluding holidays) will be allowed to all parties in the proceeding for filing a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (h) does not apply to documents filed pursuant to § 1.89, § 1.315(b) or § 1.316. Service by facsimile or electronic means is deemed equivalent to hand delivery and so does not trigger the additional 3 days. Examples show how to add 3 mailing days after computing the basic period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of applying short-period and mailing computations
rubrics_metrics.description: If both paragraphs (g) and (h) of this section are applicable, make the paragraph (g) computation before the paragraph (h) computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the short-period counting (exclude weekends/holidays per paragraph g) first, then add any mailing allowance (paragraph h) afterward; examples demonstrate application (e.g., opposition filed last day of filing period leading to sequential computations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing that falls on a holiday is due next business day
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided (e.g. § 76.1502(e) of this chapter) if, after making all the computations provided for in this section, the filing date falls on a holiday, the document shall be filed on the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Commission action must occur by a date that falls on a holiday, the action must be taken by the next business day. Example: filing date Friday Dec 25 — file next business day (Monday Dec 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific provisions control over general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where specific provisions of part 1 conflict with this section, those specific provisions of part 1 are controlling. Additionally, where § 76.1502(e) of this chapter conflicts with this section, those specific provisions of § 76.1502 are controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a specific rule elsewhere in Part 1 sets different timing/process rules, that specific rule prevails over the general computations in § 1.4; see cited sections for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's role in determining pre-7:00 p.m. deadline compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will determine whether a tendered document meets the pre-7:00 p.m. deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hand-delivered submissions where a pre-7:00 p.m. standard is referenced, the Secretary has authority to determine whether the tendered document met that deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service equivalence of facsimile/electronic to hand delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (h) service by facsimile or by electronic means shall be deemed equivalent to hand delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If served by facsimile/electronic means, the additional 3 days for mail does not apply because such service is equivalent to hand delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee must furnish mailing (and email for wireless) address
rubrics_metrics.description: Each licensee shall furnish the Commission with an address to be used by the Commission in serving documents or directing correspondence to that licensee. For licensees in the Wireless Radio Services, each licensee shall also furnish the Commission with an email address to be used by Commission for serving documents or directing correspondence to that licensee; correspondence sent to such email address is deemed to have been served on the licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless a licensee advises otherwise, the address in the most recent application will be used. Licensees are responsible for arrangements to assure prompt receipt at that address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee responsibility to assure delivery of Commission documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee is responsible for making any arrangements which may be necessary in his particular circumstances to assure that Commission documents or correspondence delivered to this address will promptly reach him or some person authorized by him to act in his behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees should maintain correct contact info and ensure staff/agents can receive Commission correspondence promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and handling of station logs and records for Commission inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Station records and logs shall be made available for inspection or duplication at the request of the Commission or its representative. Such logs or records may be removed from the licensee's possession by a Commission representative or, upon request, shall be mailed by the licensee to the Commission by either registered mail, return receipt requested, or certified mail, return receipt requested. The return receipt shall be retained by the licensee as part of the station records until such records or logs are returned to the licensee. A receipt shall be furnished when the logs or records are removed from the licensee's possession by a Commission representative and this receipt shall be retained by the licensee as part of the station records until such records or logs are returned to the licensee. When the Commission has no further need for such records or logs, they shall be returned to the licensee. The provisions of this rule shall apply solely to those station logs and records which are required to be maintained by the provisions of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If removed by staff, obtain and retain receipts; if mailed, use registered/certified mail with return receipt and retain receipt until return. Applies only to records required by the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law enforcement records exception to removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where records or logs are maintained as the official records of a recognized law enforcement agency and the removal of the records from the possession of the law enforcement agency will hinder its law enforcement activities, such records will not be removed pursuant to this section if the chief of the law enforcement agency promptly certifies in writing to the Federal Communications Commission that removal of the logs or records will hinder law enforcement activities of the agency, stating insofar as feasible the basis for his decision and the date when it can reasonably be expected that such records will be released to the Federal Communications Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law enforcement chiefs must promptly certify in writing the basis and expected release date to prevent removal; this prevents hindering law enforcement operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings and documents are filed upon receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided in this Title, by Public Notice, or by decision of the Commission or of the Commission's staff acting on delegated authority, pleadings and other documents are considered to be filed with the Commission upon their receipt at the location designated by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing occurs at receipt, not at mailing or transmission unless otherwise stated; designated locations control the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal/dismissal does not authorize removal from records
rubrics_metrics.description: The granting of a request to dismiss or withdraw an application or a pleading does not authorize the removal of such application or pleading from the Commission's records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after dismissal/withdrawal, the document remains in Commission records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to copies of submitted materials and transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person submitting data or evidence ... shall have the right to retain a copy thereof, or to procure a copy of any document submitted by him, or of any transcript made of his testimony, upon payment of the charges therefor to the person furnishing the same, which person may be designated by the Commission. The Commission itself shall not be responsible for furnishing the copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters may obtain copies but must pay any charges; the Commission need not provide the copies itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to attorneys of Commission documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In any matter pending before the Commission in which an attorney has appeared for, submitted a document on behalf of or been otherwise designated by a person, any notice or other written communication pertaining to that matter issued by the Commission and which is required or permitted to be furnished to the person will be communicated to the attorney ... For matters involving Wireless Radio Services, emailed to the attorney instead of mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission sends required notices to the attorney(s) of record; for wireless matters, email to attorney is used instead of mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for petitions for review and multiple-petition judicial lottery service
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party filing a petition for review in any United States court of appeals of a Commission Order pursuant to 47 U.S.C. 402(a) and 28 U.S.C. 2342(1), that wishes to avail itself of procedures established for selection of a court ... shall, within ten days after the issuance of that order, serve on the Office of General Counsel, by email to LitigationNotice@fcc.gov, a copy of its petition for review as filed and date-stamped by the court of appeals within which it was filed. Such copies ... must be received by the Office of General Counsel by 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time on the tenth day of the filing period. A return email ... acknowledging receipt ... will constitute proof of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely email service to LitigationNotice@fcc.gov within ten days (received by 5:30 p.m. ET on day 10) is required to participate in court-selection procedures; an acknowledgement email serves as proof of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative service method for petitions for review when email unavailable (unrepresented parties only)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party ... is unable to use email ... it shall instead, within ten days after the issuance of the order on appeal, serve a copy of its petition for review in person on the General Counsel ... Only parties not represented by counsel may use this method. Such parties must telephone the Litigation Division ... to make arrangements at 202-418-1740. Parties are advised to call at least one day before service must be effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-person service on the General Counsel is available only to pro se (unrepresented) parties who cannot use email, but they must call ahead to arrange service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of ten-day period for petitions for review governed by FRAP Rule 26
rubrics_metrics.description: Computation of time of the ten-day period for filing copies of petitions for review of a Commission order shall be governed by Rule 26 of the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure. The date of issuance of a Commission order for purposes of filing copies of petitions for review shall be the date of public notice as defined in § 1.4(b) of the Commission's Rules, 47 CFR 1.4(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FRAP Rule 26 (counting rules) and Commission 'date of public notice' definition to compute the ten-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of electronic service for notices of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of notices of appeals filed pursuant to 47 U.S.C. 402(b) shall be served upon the General Counsel. The FCC consents to—and encourages—service of such notices by email to the address LitigationNotice@fcc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email service to LitigationNotice@fcc.gov is the encouraged method for notices of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for Commission documents published in the FCC Record
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriate reference to the FCC Record shall be included as part of the citation to any document that has been printed in the Record. The citation should provide the volume, page number and year, in that order (e.g., 1 FCC Rcd. 1 (1986)). Older documents may continue to be cited to the FCC Reports ... (e.g., 1 FCC 2d 1 (1965)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite volume, page, year in that order; use FCC Reports for older printed documents as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unsworn declarations in lieu of affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document to be filed with the Federal Communications Commission and which is required ... to be supported ... by a written sworn declaration, verification, certificate, statement, oath or affidavit ... may be supported ... by the unsworn declaration, certification, verification, or statement in writing of such person, except that, such declaration shall not be used in connection with: (a) A deposition, (b) an oath of office, or (c) an oath required to be taken before a specified official other than a notary public. Such declaration shall be subscribed by the declarant as true under penalty of perjury, and dated, in substantially the following form: [form language for executed without the United States and executed within the United States].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsworn declaration may substitute for affidavit except in specified contexts; the rule provides two model statements (for inside and outside U.S.) that must be signed and dated under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful and accurate statements requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In any investigatory or adjudicatory matter ... no person subject to this rule shall: (1) In any written or oral statement of fact, intentionally provide material factual information that is incorrect or intentionally omit material information that is necessary to prevent any material factual statement that is made from being incorrect or misleading; and (2) In any written statement of fact, provide material factual information that is incorrect or omit material information that is necessary to prevent any material factual statement that is made from being incorrect or misleading without a reasonable basis for believing that any such material factual statement is correct and not misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to many categories of persons (applicants, holders, persons performing activities requiring authorization, persons subject to Commission inquiry, filings of expressions of interest in allotment proceedings, cable operators/common carriers, etc.). Intentional misstatements or omissions are prohibited; written statements must have a reasonable basis for belief in accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative dispute resolution policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has adopted an initial policy statement that supports and encourages the use of alternative dispute resolution procedures in its administrative proceedings and proceedings in which the Commission is a party ... In accordance with the Commission's policy ... procedures contained in the Administrative Dispute Resolution Act, including the provisions dealing with confidentiality, shall also be applied in Commission alternative dispute resolution proceedings in which the Commission itself is not a party to the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADR and regulatory negotiation are encouraged; confidentiality provisions from the ADR Act apply where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric units required where provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Where parenthesized English units accompany metric units throughout this chapter, and the two figures are not precisely equivalent, the metric unit shall be considered the sole requirement; except, however, that the use of metric paper sizes is not currently required, and compliance with the English unit shall be considered sufficient when the Commission form requests that data showing compliance with that particular standard be submitted in English units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When both metric and English units are shown and differ, follow metric. Paper-size metric requirement is excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appear as a party
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may appear before the Commission and be heard in person or by attorney. The appropriate Bureau Chief(s) of the Commission shall be deemed to be a party to every adjudicatory proceeding ... When, in any proceeding, a pleading is filed on behalf of either the General Counsel or the Chief Engineer, he shall thereafter be deemed a party to the proceeding. Except as otherwise expressly provided ... a duly authorized corporate officer or employee may act for the corporation in any matter which has not been designated for hearing and, in the discretion of the presiding officer, may appear and be heard on behalf of the corporation in a hearing proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may appear personally or via counsel; certain officials are automatically parties; corporate officers may act for corporations except where hearing is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for representation may be required
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, in a representative capacity, transacting business with the Commission, may be required to show his authority to act in such capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to show proof of authorization when representing others before the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be admitted to practice before the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who is a member in good standing of the bar of the Supreme Court of the United States or of the highest court of any state, territory or the District of Columbia, and who is not under any final order ... suspends, enjoins, restrains, disbars, or otherwise restricts him or her in the practice of law ... may represent others before the Commission. When such member of the bar ... appears in person or signs a paper in practice before the Commission, his personal appearance or signature shall constitute a representation to the Commission that ... he is authorized and qualified to represent the particular party ... Further proof of authority to act in a representative capacity may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar membership in the highest court and good standing are prerequisites; a signature/appearance is a representation of authority but Commission may request further proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and process for censure, suspension, or disbarment of attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may censure, suspend, or disbar any person who has practiced, is practicing or holding himself out as entitled to practice before it if it finds that such person: (1) Does not possess the qualifications required by § 1.23; (2) Has failed to conform to standards of ethical conduct required of practitioners at the bar of any court of which he is a member; (3) Is lacking in character or professional integrity; and/or (4) Displays toward the Commission or any of its hearing officers conduct which ... would be cause for censure, suspension, or disbarment. Except as provided in paragraph (c), before any member ... shall be censured, suspended, or disbarred, charges shall be preferred by the Commission ... and he or she shall be afforded an opportunity to be heard thereon. Upon receipt of official notice from any authority ... demonstrating that an attorney practicing before the Commission is subject to an order of final suspension ... the Commission may, without any preliminary hearing, enter an order temporarily suspending the attorney from practice before it pending final disposition ... Allegations of attorney misconduct ... shall be referred under seal to the Office of General Counsel. Pending action ... the decision maker may proceed with the merits but may make findings concerning the attorney's conduct only if necessary to resolve questions concerning an applicant and may not reach any conclusions regarding the ethical ramifications of the attorney's conduct. The General Counsel will determine if the allegations are substantial, and, if so, shall immediately notify the attorney and direct him or her to respond ... The General Counsel will then determine what further measures are necessary ... including recommending institution of proceedings under paragraph (a); referring the matter to the appropriate bar; or consulting with the Department of Justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists grounds for discipline, provides for notice and hearing except in certain temporary-suspension circumstances, and sets referral processes; confidentiality and procedural protections are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness rights to counsel and counsel's limited participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual compelled to appear in person in any Commission proceeding may be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel ... Counsel may advise his client in confidence ... Counsel for the witness will be permitted to make objections on the record, and to state briefly the basis for such objections, in connection with any examination of his client. At the conclusion of the examination of his client, counsel may ask clarifying questions if in the judgment of the presiding officer such questioning is necessary or desirable ... Except as provided by paragraph (c) of this section, counsel for the witness may not examine or cross-examine any witness, or offer documentary evidence, unless authorized by the Commission to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel may advise, object, and ask limited clarifying questions but generally may not examine/cross-examine or offer evidence without Commission authorization; presiding officer discretion applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal requests for Commission action content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where formal procedures are required under the provisions of this chapter, requests for action may be submitted informally. Requests should set forth clearly and concisely the facts relied upon, the relief sought, the statutory and/or regulatory provisions (if any) pursuant to which the request is filed and under which relief is sought, and the interest of the person submitting the request. In application and licensing matters pertaining to the Wireless Radio Services ... such requests must be submitted electronically, via the ULS, and the request must include an email address for receiving electronic service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal requests must include facts, relief sought, legal basis, and the filer’s interest; wireless application-related informal requests must be filed electronically via ULS and include an email for service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate pleadings required for different decisionmakers/requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests requiring action by the Commission shall not be combined in a pleading with requests for action by an administrative law judge or by any person or persons acting pursuant to delegated authority. Requests requiring action by an administrative law judge shall not be combined ... Requests requiring action by any person or persons pursuant to delegated authority shall not be combined ... Pleadings which combine requests in a manner prohibited ... may be returned without consideration to the person who filed the pleading. Any request to stay the effectiveness of any decision or order of the Commission shall be filed as a separate pleading. Any such request which is not filed as a separate pleading will not be considered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate filings are required when different decisionmakers or delegated authorities are involved; combining prohibited requests risks return without consideration; stays must be filed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings filing periods for petitions, oppositions, and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings in Commission proceedings shall be filed in accordance with the provisions of this section. (b) Oppositions to any motion, petition, or request may be filed within 10 days after the original pleading is filed. (c) The person who filed the original pleading may reply to oppositions within 5 days after the time for filing oppositions has expired. The reply shall be limited to matters raised in the oppositions, and the response to all such matters shall be set forth in a single pleading; separate replies to individual oppositions shall not be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions: 10 days; replies: 5 days after oppositions' filing period; replies limited to matters raised in oppositions and must be a single consolidated reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions to temporary relief and ex parte disposition authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions to a request for stay of any order or to a request for other temporary relief shall be filed within 7 days after the request is filed. Replies to oppositions should not be filed and will not be considered. The provisions of § 1.4(h) shall not apply in computing the filing date for oppositions to a request for stay or for other temporary relief. As a matter of discretion, the Commission may rule ex parte upon requests for continuances and extensions of time, requests for permission to file pleadings in excess of the length prescribed in this chapter, and requests for temporary relief, without waiting for the filing of oppositions or replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary relief oppositions: 7 days; replies not considered; mailing-additional-days rule doesn't apply; Commission may act ex parte on certain procedural requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for extension of time policy and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the Commission that extensions of time shall not be routinely granted. Motions for extension of time in which to file responses to petitions for rulemaking, replies to such responses, comments filed in response to notice of proposed rulemaking, replies to such comments and other filings in rulemaking proceedings conducted under Subpart C of this part shall be filed at least 7 days before the filing date. If a timely motion is denied, the responses and comments, replies thereto, or other filings need not be filed until 2 business days after the Commission acts on the motion. In emergency situations, the Commission will consider a late-filed motion for a brief extension of time related to the duration of the emergency and will consider motions for acceptance of comments, reply comments or other filings made after the filing date. If a motion for extension of time in which to make filings in proceedings other than notice and comment rule making proceedings is filed less than 7 days prior to the filing day, the party filing the motion shall (in addition to serving the motion on other parties) orally notify other parties and Commission staff personnel responsible for acting on the motion that the motion has been (or is being) filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are disfavored; for rulemaking-related filings, file extension motions ≥7 days before filing date; if denied, filings due 2 business days after Commission action; emergencies may justify late motions; for non-rulemaking late motions (<7 days), oral notice to parties and responsible staff is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of documents and proof of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commission or any person is required by statute or by the provisions of this chapter to serve any document upon any person, service shall (in the absence of specific provisions in this chapter to the contrary) be made in accordance with the provisions of this section. Where any person is required to serve any document filed with the Commission, service shall be made by that person or by his representative on or before the day on which the document is filed. Commission counsel who formally participate in any proceeding shall be served in the same manner as other persons who participate in that proceeding. The filing of a document with the Commission does not constitute service upon Commission counsel. Except in formal complaint proceedings against common carriers ... and proceedings related to the Wireless Radio Services under subpart F of this part, documents may be served upon a party, his attorney, or other duly constituted agent by delivering a copy or by mailing a copy to the last known address. Documents that are required to be served must be served in paper form, even if documents are filed in electronic form with the Commission, unless the party to be served agrees to accept service in some other form. Petitions, pleadings, and other documents associated with licensing matters in the Wireless Radio Services must be served electronically upon a party, his attorney, or other duly constituted agent by delivering a copy by email to the email address listed in the Universal Licensing System (ULS). If a filer is not an applicant or licensee, the document must include an email address for receiving electronic service. Delivery of a copy pursuant to this section means handing it to the party, his attorney, or other duly constituted agent; or leaving it with the clerk or other person in charge of the office of the person being served; or, if there is no one in charge of such office, leaving it in a conspicuous place therein; or, if such office is closed or the person to be served has no office, leaving it at his dwelling house or usual place of abode with some person of suitable age and discretion then residing therein. For pleadings, petitions, and other documents associated with licensing matters in the Wireless Radio Services, delivery of a copy pursuant to this section is complete by sending it by email to the email addresses listed in the ULS, or to the email address of the applicant's or licensee's attorney provided in a pleading or other document served on the filer. Service by mail is complete upon mailing. Service by email is complete upon sending to the email address listed in the ULS for a particular license, application, or filing. Proof of service ... shall be filed before action is taken. The proof of service shall show the time and manner of service, and may be by written acknowledgement of service, by certificate of the person effecting the service, or by other proof satisfactory to the Commission. Failure to make proof of service will not affect the validity of the service. The Commission may allow the proof to be amended or supplied at any time, unless to do so would result in material prejudice to a party. Proof of electronic service shall show the email address of the person making the service, in addition to that person's residence or business address; the date and time of the electronic service; the name and email address of the person served; and that the document was served electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must generally occur on or before the day of filing; paper service is required in many contexts unless party agrees otherwise; wireless licensing matters use ULS email addresses for service; proof of service must be submitted before action and must include detailed information for electronic service; proofs can be amended unless prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agent in District of Columbia for carriers and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every common carrier and interconnected VoIP provider ... and non-interconnected VoIP provider ... that is subject to the Communications Act ... shall designate an agent in the District of Columbia, and may designate additional agents ... Such designation shall include, for the carrier, interconnected VoIP provider, or non-interconnected VoIP provider and its designated agents, a name, business address, telephone or voicemail number, facsimile number, and, if available, internet email address. Such carrier ... shall additionally list any other names by which it is known or under which it does business, and, if the carrier ... is an affiliated company, the parent, holding, or management company. Within thirty (30) days of the commencement of provision of service, such carrier ... shall file such information with the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau's Market Disputes Resolution Division. Such carriers ... may file a hard copy of the relevant portion of the Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet ... to satisfy the requirement ... Each Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet filed annually ... must contain a name, business address, telephone or voicemail number, facsimile number, and, if available, internet email address for its designated agents, regardless of whether such information has been revised since the previous filing. Carriers ... must notify the Commission within one week of any changes in their designation information by filing revised portions of the Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet with the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau's Market Disputes Resolution Division. A paper copy of this designation list shall be maintained in the Office of the Secretary of the Commission. Service of any notice, process, orders, decisions or requirements of the Commission may be made upon such carrier ... by leaving a copy thereof with such designated agent at his office or usual place of residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carriers and certain VoIP providers must designate DC agent(s) with full contact details and file the information within 30 days of commencing service; update within one week of changes; maintain a paper copy in the Office of the Secretary; service on the designated agent constitutes service on the carrier.
